title: Crond
subtitle: Scheduled jobs — flip for meaning, crontab examples, and notes

cards.meaning: cron = the clock daemon; crontab = that user’s schedule file
cards.example: Edit with crontab -e, not a random text file (unless admin on system files)
cards.notes: Together they run “every night at 2am” without a human at the keyboard. systemd unit: crond.service / cron.service.

cards.meaning: Edit the current user’s crontab in $EDITOR
cards.notes: Supported way to change user jobs. Spool files live under /var/spool/cron (RHEL) or /var/spool/cron/crontabs (Debian).
User jobs are named after accounts in /etc/passwd.

cards.meaning: minute hour day-of-month month weekday, then the command
cards.notes: Ranges: min 0–59, hour 0–23, dom 1–31, month 1–12, weekday 0–7 (0 and 7 = Sunday). Cron’s finest grain is one minute.

cards.meaning: System crontab line: five time fields, then a username, then the command
cards.notes: User crontabs omit the username field. System drop-ins in /etc/cron.d/ use a different format from personal crontabs.

cards.meaning: User crontab files, named after accounts; loaded into memory
cards.example: File named alice holds alice’s jobs
cards.notes: Memory hook: user jobs = spool dir. System jobs = /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.d/.

cards.meaning: Drop scripts here to run on that cadence without writing a five-field line
cards.notes: Run via a system cron/anacron hook. /etc/anacrontab is for jobs that should still run if the machine was off.
Also: 5,17 = 5 and 17; */10 = every 10; jan,may or sun,fri allowed.
*/n is a step in whichever field it sits (minutes, hours, …).
Comma = list of values in one field.
Weekday names work. Also: 0 17 * * sun,fri for Sun and Fri.

cards.meaning: First Sunday of the month at 02:00
cards.notes: Cron cannot say “first Sunday” alone — 0 2 * * sun is every Sunday; the date test keeps only days 1–7.

cards.meaning: Two cron lines: the job at second 0, and sleep 30; same job
cards.notes: Cron has no sub-minute field. Finest grain is one minute.

cards.meaning: Job stdout/stderr is mailed to the crontab owner, or to MAILTO if set
cards.notes: Redirect yourself with >> log 2>&1 to avoid mail. With cron -s, output can also go to syslog.

cards.meaning: Every four hours, on the hour
